title: membrane record
description: A membrane record (data/standards/assets/<name>.dat or a case's constant/assets/<name>.dat, `kind NF;` / `RO;` / ...), as src/thermo/membrane/Membrane.cpp (Membrane::readFromDict) reads it: the solution-diffusion permeances every membrane law can use and, in an optional `poreModel {}` block, the charged-pore geometry the DSPM-DE transport law needs.  This schema is the GUI's reading aid for F1 in the Case tab (DEV.md 4c C154); the reader is the engine, and a key it does not read refuses there.

name.title: Record name
name.description: The word a case names the membrane by (`membrane <name>;`); the file is <name>.dat.

kind.title: Membrane kind
kind.description: NF, RO, ... -- the family of the membrane, what a module or bench checks it against.

manufacturer.title: Manufacturer
manufacturer.description: Who makes it, or what it is when nobody does (a program's worked example).

A_w.title: Pure-water permeance A_w
A_w.description: J_w = A_w (dP - dpi): the water flux per unit of net driving pressure.  REQUIRED by the record grammar.  A unit that IMPOSES the permeate flux J_v (the props bench `poreTransport`) does not read it: there is no J_w = A_w (dP - dpi) closure there, and the engine says so at every point (`[DSPM-DE] J_v IMPOSED by the caller`).

P_max.title: Maximum pressure
P_max.description: The manufacturer's limit, when stated; 0 = none declared.

T_max.title: Maximum temperature
T_max.description: The manufacturer's limit, when stated; 0 = none declared.

pH_min.title: Minimum pH
pH_min.description: The manufacturer's limit, when stated; 0 = none declared.

pH_max.title: Maximum pH
pH_max.description: The manufacturer's limit, when stated; 0 = none declared.

MWCO.title: Molecular-weight cut-off
MWCO.description: The manufacturer's nominal cut-off, when stated.

permeabilities.title: Solute permeances B_s
permeabilities.description: Per solute (component name -> B_s): the solution-diffusion salt flux J_s = B_s (c_wall - c_perm).  Read by the solution-diffusion laws, not by DSPM-DE (which solves the pore instead).

poreModel.title: DSPM-DE pore model
poreModel.description: The Donnan-steric-dielectric pore the DSPM-DE transport law solves across (Bowen & Mohammad; Geraldes & Alves 2008 for NanoFiltran).  `poreRadius` and either `porosityOverThickness` or both `porosity` and `thickness` are MANDATORY when the block is present; `chargeDensity` and `poreDielectric` are optional (absent: steric only / Born off).  A membrane without this block cannot select DSPM-DE.

poreRadius.title: Pore radius r_p
poreRadius.description: The radius of the cylindrical pore of the active layer (raw SI metres).  It is the MEMBRANE's radius, not a solute's: each ion enters through its ratio lambda = r_i/r_p (r_i the `radius` the ion's species record carries -- the one number the model reads, whatever convention produced it: the standard catalogue's are hydrated radii (Nightingale 1959), and a case-local record may carry another and says so in its header, e.g. the Stokes radii of the NanoFiltran paper's case), which sets the steric partition Phi = (1 - lambda)^2 and the hindrance factors K_d, K_c (Dechadilok & Deen 2006); an ion with lambda >= 1 is excluded.  (The Born dielectric exclusion uses the ION's radius, not this one: see `poreDielectric`.)  DIRECTION, at the partition level: a larger r_p lowers every lambda, so Phi_S and K_d rise toward 1 and the pore tells ions apart less by size.  WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: which way a REJECTION moves.  In a mixture the observed rejection is not monotone in this parameter -- the counter-ions compete for the fixed charge across the pore, so a trace counter-ion's rejection can change sign and a co-ion can be negatively rejected (tutorials/props/membrane/nanofiltran_geraldesAlves2008: Na+ with J_v in example_ideal, Cl- beside the dye in study B).  For a given feed the answer is a run with the value changed, not a sentence.

porosityOverThickness.title: A_k / dx
porosityOverThickness.description: Porosity over active-layer thickness: the flux per unit MEMBRANE area is the flux per unit pore area times A_k/dx, so its inverse dx/A_k is the equivalent thickness the extended Nernst-Planck equations are integrated across.  Alternatively declare `porosity` and `thickness`.  DIRECTION, at the transport level: a larger A_k/dx raises each ion's diffusive conductance K_d D_i A_k/dx, so at a given J_v its Peclet number Pe_i = K_c J_v / (K_d D_i A_k/dx) falls -- diffusion gains on convection across the pore.  WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: which way a REJECTION moves.  In a mixture the observed rejection is not monotone in this parameter -- the counter-ions compete for the fixed charge across the pore, so a trace counter-ion's rejection can change sign and a co-ion can be negatively rejected (tutorials/props/membrane/nanofiltran_geraldesAlves2008: Na+ with J_v in example_ideal, Cl- beside the dye in study B).  For a given feed the answer is a run with the value changed, not a sentence.

chargeDensity.title: Fixed charge X_d
chargeDensity.description: The membrane's effective fixed charge per pore volume, SIGNED (negative for a negatively charged membrane).  It enters the Donnan partition at both faces and electroneutrality in the pore.  Absent: steric only.  A props `poreTransport` op may replace it for that op only (`chargeDensity` in the op), announced.  DIRECTION, at the partition level: a larger |X_d| deepens the Donnan jump at both faces, so each face's Donnan factor exp(-z_i F dpsi_D/RT) falls further below 1 for a co-ion (the sign of X_d) and rises further above 1 for a counter-ion -- LINEAR in z_i in the exponent, so a divalent co-ion is pushed out twice as hard as a monovalent one.  WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: which way a REJECTION moves.  In a mixture the observed rejection is not monotone in this parameter -- the counter-ions compete for the fixed charge across the pore, so a trace counter-ion's rejection can change sign and a co-ion can be negatively rejected (tutorials/props/membrane/nanofiltran_geraldesAlves2008: Na+ with J_v in example_ideal, Cl- beside the dye in study B).  For a given feed the answer is a run with the value changed, not a sentence.

poreDielectric.title: Pore dielectric constant eps_p
poreDielectric.description: Relative permittivity inside the pore; below the bulk value it excludes ions by the Born solvation energy z_i^2 e^2 / (8 pi eps_0 r_i) (1/eps_p - 1/eps_b), r_i the ion's own radius -- both signs alike, divalent ions four times as strongly.  Absent: Born off.  Must be > 0.  DIRECTION, at the partition level: a lower eps_p raises dW_i for both signs alike, as z_i^2, so the Born factor exp(-dW_i/kT) falls for every ion, and four times as fast in the exponent for a divalent one.  WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: which way a REJECTION moves.  In a mixture the observed rejection is not monotone in this parameter -- the counter-ions compete for the fixed charge across the pore, so a trace counter-ion's rejection can change sign and a co-ion can be negatively rejected (tutorials/props/membrane/nanofiltran_geraldesAlves2008: Na+ with J_v in example_ideal, Cl- beside the dye in study B).  For a given feed the answer is a run with the value changed, not a sentence.

fit.title: Fit provenance
fit.description: Written by a Properties-mode fit (DEV.md 4c C152): the fingerprints of the inputs that produced this record; Process mode refuses the record when they no longer match.
